nominative noun

also nominative case, in the nominative, give the nominative

classical

Quint. 1.7.3: eadem littera nōminātīvō cāsū brevis, ablātīvō longa est
Varr. LL 10.23 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 221, 247

nōminātīvus, nōminātīvī m.

noun, second declension

the nominative case

Short for cāsus nōminātīvus, the naming case; the adjective may stand alone. Quintilian also calls it the upright case, rēctus cāsus (1.5.61).

Other words

  • rēctus cāsus — the nominative, the “upright” case

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.5.61: masculīna Graeca nōmina rēctō cāsū

Examples

  • cum eadem littera nōminātīvō cāsū brevis, ablātīvō longa est

    when the same letter is short in the nominative and long in the ablativeQuint. 1.7.3

  • Dīc cāsum nōminātīvum.

    Give the nominative case.Traupman 240

See also case, genitive, subject.

SourcesLewis & Short: nominativus · Lewis & Short: rectus
